answer: Epoch 120: Standing grows through irreversible branching choices. Each identity must commit, on-ledger, to one mutually exclusive path - hauling ferrous ore, guarding a saffron store, or tracking a sparrow migration - and that choice closes the other paths while shaping which tasks it can take next. A sybil operator faces a fork: copy one choice across clones and they crowd the same path, splitting its reward and exposing correlation; or decide separately for each clone, so reasoning costs scale per identity and late clones cannot fabricate the time-ordered history they skipped.
